Recall and apply principle facts facts in exam-style questions.
Match=expense timing, accrual=when earned, going concern=continues, entity=separate, money measurement=monetary only.
Matching vs accrual and entity vs going concern are the most mixed-up pairs.
Accrual accounting recognises revenue when earned and expenses when incurred.
Going concern lets assets be valued at cost because the business is not being liquidated.
Consistency lets financial statements be compared across years.
Prudence recognises losses early but profits only when realised.
True/false stems on principles.
Because "The matching principle links expenses to the revenue they earn." states the correct fact, while the other statements are deliberately false.
